Stage 3 native R preprocessing, kinematics and trajectory distances

etr_native_preprocessing_distances.Rd

Seven independently implemented R functions, corresponding to published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 public functions. These implementations do not execute Python. Independent Python numerical oracles are provided separately as optional tests; numerical/generalized equivalence is not automatically certified by installation.

Usage

etr_normalize_coordinates(x, width, height,
                          python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_center_on_landmark(x, landmark_x, landmark_y,
                       python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_normalize_time_interval(x, start = 0, end = 1,
                            python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_heading_function(x, dimensions = NULL, min_speed = 0,
                     undefined_policy = c("nan", "raise"))
etr_trajectory_tortuosity_frame(x, dimensions = NULL, min_displacement = 0,
                                undefined_policy = c("nan", "raise"))
etr_pairwise_frechet(x, dimensions = NULL, dimension_weights = NULL,
                     python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_nearest_trajectory_indices(x, index, n_neighbors = 5L,
                               python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

Arguments

x

An etr_trajectory_set with common, strictly increasing time values. Derivative and distance functions may require complete observations.

width, height

Strictly positive finite coordinate extents.

landmark_x, landmark_y

Finite scalars or numeric vectors with one landmark per curve.

start, end

Finite new time interval endpoints, with end>start.

dimensions

Optional ordered distinct named channel selection. Planar methods default to channels x and y only if explicitly present. Pairwise Frechet defaults to all stored channels.

min_speed

Non-negative lower speed limit (undefined when speed<=min_speed).

undefined_policy

"nan" maps undefined Python numeric results to NA_real_; "raise" stops on undefined samples/curves.

min_displacement

Nonnegative endpoint displacement threshold.

dimension_weights

Optional finite non-negative channel weights, containing at least one strictly positive value. In explicit source-boundary mode, Fréchet also accepts numeric-compatible logical and string weights.

index

Zero-based integer target curve index, matching Python's nearest_trajectory_indices().

n_neighbors

Positive integer number of nearest distinct curves. Requesting more than exist returns all available distinct curves.

python_boundary_mode

Logical opt-in to bounded Python 1.2 source-domain semantics for coordinate normalization, time normalization, landmark centering and nearest-neighbor slicing. Boolean coordinate extents (TRUE = 1, FALSE invalid) and Boolean time endpoints are converted for native numerical operations. Landmark centering accepts finite numeric-string and Boolean inputs through NumPy-like scalar or per-curve conversions; invalid strings and nonfinite values remain unsupported. Nearest-neighbor counts follow Python's Boolean/integer slice-index rules. Pairwise Fréchet accepts bounded finite NumPy-style dimension weights but retains native R distance computations and results. FALSE preserves strict native R defaults; no Python bridge is used.

Value

The first four functions return a native etr_trajectory_set; etr_trajectory_tortuosity_frame() returns a base R data.frame; etr_pairwise_frechet() returns a symmetric numeric distance matrix without dimnames; etr_nearest_trajectory_indices() returns zero-based integer indices.

Details

Coordinate normalization divides only the first two stored channels by width/height without clipping out-of-bounds gaze or modifying other channels. Centering subtracts explicitly supplied per-curve landmarks, not a trajectory's mean or first location. Time normalization accepts arbitrary valid endpoints and does not alter values.

Heading is wrapped atan2(v_y,v_x) computed using the same second-order edge-aware nonuniform-grid derivative as the Python reference. Tortuosity reports sampled path length divided by endpoint displacement with the same inclusive zero-denominator rule as the Python reference. Pairwise Frechet uses ordered point sequences, not elapsed time, in the discrete dynamic-programming recurrence.

As of native Stage 5, etr_trajectory_set() can retain a JSON-like native R provenance mapping, and Stage 3 normalization and landmark centering append their documented audit fields without Python. This does not qualify all Python source-schema details or serialization. The native tortuosity data frame still omits the Python pandas DataFrame.attrs provenance field. Full behavioral and schema parity remain open. For nearest-neighbor distance ties, the native R version uses ascending original index; Python NumPy's default argsort tie ordering may differ.

Examples

tt <- c(0,.2,.6,1,2)
a <- array(0,c(2,length(tt),2))
a[1,,1] <- tt
a[1,,2] <- tt^2
a[2,,1] <- tt+1
a[2,,2] <- tt^2+1
x <- etr_trajectory_set(tt,a,dimension_names=c("x","y"),
                        coordinate_system="pixels")
y <- etr_normalize_coordinates(x,1920,1080)
z <- etr_center_on_landmark(x,1,1)
p <- etr_pairwise_frechet(x)
